technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Rabbit sink batching as an opt-in configuration property, with batchingEnabled defaulting to false and batchingSize defaulting to 100.
Use the Rabbit client batching API and flush batches when the configured size is reached; ensure pending records are flushed on shutdown and error paths.
Preserve existing one-at-a-time Rabbit sink behavior when batching is disabled, including existing acknowledgment and error semantics.
Add a Gradle build option for module projects using Spring XD dependencies with provided-like dependency scoping and Spring Boot MODULE layout configuration.
Expose compression configuration through an injectable or overridable compression strategy/factory rather than hard-coding the current default implementation.
Add hdfs-dataset acceptance tests to the existing CI test lifecycle, using the project-supported embedded or test Hadoop environment.
Make database initialization conditional so DIRT runtime can start without database infrastructure when stream processing does not require persistence.
Define and implement the core processor interface contract required by RxJava-based processor modules while preserving compatibility with existing module contracts.
Use the existing project test framework, build conventions, Rabbit test infrastructure, and benchmark harness wherever available rather than introducing replacement tooling.
Treat benchmark reruns as reproducible test activities and record configuration, throughput, latency, and comparison results as project benchmark artifacts.
assumptions: The existing repository, build, CI configuration, Rabbit sink, compression code, DIRT runtime, hdfs-dataset module, and benchmark harness are available and buildable.
The implementation targets the repository's existing Spring Framework and Java compatibility level; upgrading Spring, Java, Rabbit, Hadoop, or RxJava versions is out of scope.

One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused development effort by one developer; estimates include implementation, local verification, and normal debugging but not elapsed waiting time.
The Rabbit broker and Hadoop test dependencies can be run using existing local, embedded, containerized, or CI-supported infrastructure without provisioning a new production environment.
Acceptance tests are expected to validate the primary hdfs-dataset workflows and integrate with CI; extensive distributed-cluster fault-injection testing is out of scope.
The Gradle requirement is limited to adding the supported build option and required boilerplate, not migrating the entire project from its existing build system.
Compression customization requires overriding the existing default codec or strategy through configuration or dependency injection; implementation of new compression algorithms is out of scope.
Performance benchmarks can be rerun with existing benchmark data-generation, measurement, and reporting scripts; new benchmark methodology is not required.

Disabling the database requirement applies only to DIRT startup and stream-processing scenarios that do not need persistent metadata; database-dependent features must continue to fail or be rejected clearly when invoked without a database.
The RxJava processor interface contract can be implemented using the RxJava version already present in the project, without a major reactive API migration.
No external product management, security audit, performance lab provisioning, or independent tester effort is included; all listed work is performed by the implementing developer.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build files, Rabbit sink, compression abstractions, DIRT startup path, hdfs-dataset tests, RxJava integration, CI jobs, and benchmark harness; identify integration points and define the implementation sequence.

Add batchingEnabled and batchingSize configuration, implement accumulation and flush behavior, handle shutdown and error-path flushing, and preserve existing non-batched delivery and acknowledgment semantics for U1.

activities.activity_name: Rabbit batching unit and integration tests
activities.activity_description: Add tests for disabled and enabled modes, batch-size boundaries, partial final batches, shutdown flushing, failures, acknowledgments, configuration defaults, and compatibility with existing Rabbit sink behavior.

Add the Gradle build option and conventions needed for module projects, including dependency scoping, Spring Boot MODULE layout configuration, generated or shared boilerplate, and validation with a representative module project for U2.

Refactor or extend compression setup so the default compressor remains unchanged while users can override the codec, strategy, or factory through supported configuration or dependency injection for U4.
Test default compression behavior, custom implementation selection, configuration validation, serialization and decompression compatibility, and failure handling for U4.

Create end-to-end acceptance scenarios for the hdfs-dataset module, configure required test data and Hadoop services, assert expected dataset operations, and integrate the tests with the standard CI build for U3.

Configure the existing benchmark suite with batchingEnabled=true and batchingSize=100, execute baseline comparisons, capture throughput and latency results, optionally run selected alternate batch sizes, and record the results for U5.

Enable compression in the existing Rabbit benchmark scenarios, rerun the baseline workload, compare results with previous performance snapshots, and record relevant throughput, latency, and resource observations for U6.

Add configuration and startup branching to allow DIRT stream-processing use cases to run without database initialization while retaining database setup for features that require persistence, including useful configuration errors.

Add unit and integration coverage for database-disabled startup, database-enabled startup, persistence-dependent operations, missing or invalid configuration, and regression of existing runtime behavior for U7.

Define or complete the core interface contract required by RxJava processor modules, implement the adapter or execution path, connect lifecycle and error semantics, and provide a representative processor implementation for U8.

activities.activity_name: RxJava contract tests and compatibility verification
activities.activity_description: Test processor creation, reactive input and output, completion, backpressure or subscription behavior as supported by the existing API, error propagation, lifecycle handling, and compatibility with existing module contracts for U8.
Update CI job definitions, test profiles, configuration reference material, user-facing examples, migration notes, and benchmark result documentation for the completed user stories.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature integration and final regression verification
activities.activity_description: Run the full build and test suite, verify interactions among Rabbit configuration, compression, Gradle module packaging, DIRT startup, acceptance tests, and RxJava modules, fix discovered regressions, and finalize deliverables.
